mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the rank information coefficient over triggered periods is not statistically significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over six months signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST 6-month change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate in at least one observed recessionary episode.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months, accompanied by a decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 per month for two months, signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.5% for 3 consecutive months AND PAYEMS monthly change < -100000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate during an NBER-defined recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 3% over six months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue and profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where INDPRO declines by more than 3% over six months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals an aggressive monetary easing, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate during a period of coordinated global financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 3% over six months signals strengthening aggregate demand, which expands corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a documented early-cycle recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for six consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate during a period of documented labor market overheating.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 2% over three months signals a synchronized expansion in supply and demand, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity prices, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate during a documented economic rebound.
